# Android integration

## Add the library

Copy `android/phone-pc-bridge.aar` to your app module's `libs/` directory. Use your existing Android build; no new app or bridge frontend is required. For Kotlin Gradle DSL:

```kotlin
android {
    compileSdk = 36
    defaultConfig {
        minSdk = 33
        ndk { abiFilters += "arm64-v8a" }
    }
    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
    }
}
dependencies {
    implementation(files("libs/phone-pc-bridge.aar"))
}
```

Keep the AAR's manifest and consumer ProGuard rules. It includes INTERNET/ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE for the embedded client and network callbacks. The app owns scheduling and lifecycle; the SDK declares no foreground service, alarm or boot receiver. Do not add a phone-wide VPN or make ordinary sockets call the private hostname: requests must pass through the embedded client. The private overlay encrypts the underlying HTTP connection. The SDK manages its own transport; Android cleartext exceptions for unrelated networking are not required.

## Initialize and enroll

Run all synchronous SDK calls on a worker thread. The application owns operation cancellation, UI state and lifecycle. Share one client for the whole app process:

```java
Client client = BridgeRecovery.client(context, "stemwise-bridge", true);
// Studywell uses its own app installation and e.g. "studywell-bridge".
JSONObject transport = new JSONObject(client.status());
```

For an app that permits Bridge only on unmetered Wi-Fi, use `BridgeRecovery.client(context, "stemwise-bridge", true)` consistently, including offline local recovery. The two-argument factory selects the default active-network policy. The policy belongs to the one shared node and cannot be changed by another factory call in the same process; per-operation cancellation does not own or suspend the node's background sockets.

The Wi-Fi-only policy requires Android's active network to be validated, explicitly unmetered Wi-Fi, with neither cellular nor VPN transport; Android's active-metered classifier must also agree. Every underlying control, peer, relay, STUN and DNS socket is bound to that exact `Network` using Android's per-socket binding. DNS uses that network's literal LinkProperties DNS servers and has no default-network fallback. System/environment proxy paths and remote engine log uploads are disabled in the Android runtime. Other app traffic is unaffected.

Policy loss or replacement of the approved network revokes new socket creation, cancels in-flight network calls and synchronously closes the old embedded node. Enrollment, accepted Pi jobs, immutable request IDs and local cache deadlines survive. When approved Wi-Fi returns, the callback permits a later SDK network call to start a fresh node over the same enrollment directory; it neither starts the node nor replays requests. A lost acknowledgment still needs reconciliation using the original IDs. Before sending a new mutation, the app must retain its own user approval and workflow state.

If policy prevents startup, remote calls throw the existing structured pre-send exception with `code:"bridge_network_unavailable"`, `requestSent:false` and `retryable:true`. This is permission to wait for an approved route, not permission to replay a workflow. The factory and local file methods remain available while blocked. The low-level `Client.setNetworkEnabled(false)` suspends all node sockets while preserving local storage; setting true only permits a later call. Apps using `BridgeRecovery` leave route restoration to its network owner. Do not install a second `BridgeNetwork`, replace its socket binder, or toggle a closed shared client.

`BridgeRecovery.client` creates/reuses the app-private `getNoBackupFilesDir()/bridge-node` and supplies Android network callbacks without starting the engine. It is the shared process-owned client factory; background job resumption belongs to the app's scheduler. `client.start()`, `status()`, `login()` and remote operations may start networking; local file recovery does not require them. Do not close its shared client from an Activity or create another client over the same directory. Keep calls in the owning app process, not multiple Android processes. Node names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; stable identity comes from private state, not the name. Never copy `bridge-node` between installations or back it up.

Engine startup is not peer readiness. Before each remote JSON request or streamed file exchange, the SDK waits up to **10 seconds**, within the operation's remaining deadline, for an enrolled local identity and the exact paired peer's usable address. It polls only local status at 200 ms intervals; it does not consume upload bytes or dial the remote endpoint while waiting. Do not add an arbitrary startup sleep or require a successful status poll before making the first call. A ready peer map does not prove that the Pi/PC application is reachable; the subsequent HTTP exchange can still fail.

A failed local engine startup retires its partial node and network context; it does not publish the client as started. A later explicit SDK call can retry construction on the same client and private enrollment directory. No enrollment reset, job replay or retry loop occurs. Confirmed node retirement clears its stale stop error; unconfirmed cleanup remains a startup refusal. Local file recovery remains available independently. File listings pin storage lifetime and lock briefly for validation or one object's metadata/expiry, check cancellation through cursor traversal and before returning, and do not block concurrent uploads during full-inventory sorting. Listings are advisory under concurrent mutation; a later page can reconcile additions/removals.

For initial authorization, use your app's enrollment action to call `client.login()`, then obtain `loginUrl` from `client.status()` and present it through the app's normal HTTPS account authorization flow. Validate an HTTPS Tailscale authorization URL before opening it; do not log or persist authorization URLs in job logs. Use the owner's same bridge account and complete device approval when required. Preserve the existing state when enrollment expires or connectivity is temporarily absent. Do not retry login or reset state on every network failure.

`backendState=Running` alone is not proof of enrollment or Pi/PC reachability. The current app endpoint is:

```text
Pi host:     bridge-pi.tail49b679.ts.net
Pi identity: nfPvZiSdpi11CNTRL
PC identity: nUneuZUkvw11CNTRL
```

These host/identity values are pairing metadata, not credentials. Pin them in the integration. The SDK resolves current addresses from its enrolled peer map. Normal private account/device authorization remains necessary.

## Connection and HTTP results

```java
JSONObject wire = new JSONObject(client.callApp(operationId,
    "bridge-pi.tail49b679.ts.net", "nfPvZiSdpi11CNTRL",
    "GET", "/v2/connection", ""));
int httpStatus = wire.getInt("httpStatus");
JSONObject response = wire.getJSONObject("response");
JSONObject data = response.getJSONObject("data");
```

Check protocol and paired identities, then the HTTP status. Error responses have `data.code`, `message`, `retryable`, `action`; SDK exceptions are transport/local errors, separate from HTTP replies. `operationId` correlates/cancels this local SDK operation. It is distinct from the durable `requestId` inside a submitted job. For scheduled cancellable work, reserve `Operation phase = client.newOperation()` before publishing/scheduling the worker and pass `phase.token()` as operationId. Use one fresh lease per SDK call; cancel the lease and owned FutureTask, and close unused/rejected leases or close in the actual worker finally block. Do not rely on cancellation of a caller-generated ID before SDK entry. See SOURCE_BUILD.md for the exact atomic host handoff. `client.cancel(operationId)` cancels the entire active synchronous SDK call, including local copying/hashing and all internal requests. Cancellation stays latched across its internal stages until that call retires; it does not cancel a server job. Closed SDK-issued tokens are refused rather than adopted as fresh calls. Plain unknown IDs are not cancellation tombstones. Keep a separate app-owned cancellation flag across different SDK calls and check it before starting each phase. Server cancellation uses the job cancel endpoint and requires an authoritative terminal observation.

Readiness failures have a JSON **exception message**, not an HTTP response:

```json
{"bridgeTransportError":"v1","code":"paired_peer_map_pending","phase":"pre_send","requestSent":false,"retryable":true}
```

`requestSent:false` applies only to the failed HTTP exchange. A multi-stage SDK call may already have completed earlier exchanges or local work. `BridgeUsage.preSendTransportFailure(exception)` parses this exact envelope and returns null for an unrecognized exception. `retryable:true` allows the app to consider a bounded later attempt while its approved workflow is still active; it never schedules a retry, approves a job, renews a cancelled operation or authorizes wake. Use a new operation lease but preserve the original immutable job envelope or transfer descriptor/ID. For file recovery, use `ensureSent` so the original receipt is checked again.

`bridge_transport_starting`, `paired_peer_map_pending`, `bridge_status_unavailable` and `bridge_readiness_timeout` identify pending local readiness. Known identity/DNS/owner conflicts, duplicate identities, invalid addresses, stopped transport and expired enrollment are refused without dialing; Connection.connect returns the original nonretryable readiness failure after its first probe instead of polling until a generic timeout; repair pairing or use the existing enrollment flow rather than selecting a different peer or resetting state. Readiness cancellation can return `bridge_operation_cancelled`; other cancellation entry points may return an ordinary cancellation exception. Always preserve the app's cancellation latch. An exception without a validated no-send envelope provides no no-send evidence. Once an HTTP attempt starts, the SDK never retries it automatically: an upload/POST with a lost acknowledgment remains uncertain. Reconcile the original job/receipt instead of replaying the mutation, including after cancellation or process restart. HTTP error replies remain separate structured server results.

The complete readiness code vocabulary is below. These are transport exception codes, separate from the server's HTTP error catalog. `retryable` describes readiness only; it never authorizes replay of a previous exchange or mutation.

| Code | retryable | Meaning / recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bridge_transport_starting` | true | Local backend or self map is still starting; a bounded later attempt may succeed. |
| `paired_peer_map_pending` | true | Exact peer entry, ownership/DNS metadata or addresses are not yet available. |
| `bridge_status_unavailable` | true | Local status read was unavailable during the bounded wait. |
| `bridge_readiness_timeout` | true | Deadline elapsed before a more specific readiness reason was observed. |
| `paired_target_invalid` | false | Invalid paired hostname or stable identity; repair the stored pair. |
| `paired_identity_mismatch` | false | Target is self or the hostname belongs to another known stable identity. |
| `paired_identity_ambiguous` | false | Multiple peer entries claim the paired stable identity. |
| `paired_dns_mismatch` | false | Paired stable identity has a different known hostname. |
| `paired_owner_mismatch` | false | Known paired peer and local node belong to different owners. |
| `paired_address_invalid` | false | Peer has addresses but none is a permitted tailnet address. |
| `paired_device_enrollment_expired` | false | Paired device enrollment expired; repair that device's enrollment. |
| `bridge_enrollment_required` | false | Local login/enrollment is required or expired; use embedded enrollment. |
| `bridge_device_approval_required` | false | Local device requires owner approval in the existing enrollment flow. |
| `bridge_transport_stopped` | false | Local transport is stopped; restore its lifecycle before another request. |
| `bridge_transport_unavailable` | false | Backend state is unsupported/unavailable; retain the exact code for investigation. |
| `bridge_operation_cancelled` | false | Caller cancelled readiness; preserve cancellation and do not resume automatically. |

A deadline normally preserves the last observed reason. Brief signed startup enrollment/approval states get bounded readiness grace; a persistent state returns its original nonretryable enrollment/approval code. Known pairing conflicts are refused before startup grace.

Use a local monotonic observation deadline, conservatively subtracting request elapsed time from `validForMs`. `observedAt` is remote diagnostic context, not a phone/server wall-clock agreement requirement. Do not extend freshness after a phone clock change or assume an already delayed response is fresh. Pi reachability, PC reachability, `codexAuth`, `expiredJobCleanup` and `chatCleanup` are separate. `codexAuth.validForMs=0` means a point-in-time authentication observation; the PC independently gates every new mutation. Show its fixed machine code and preserve queued jobs during sign-in/change recovery. Provider authentication does not prove model entitlement or available quota. Do not display a requested setting as applied until the owning API confirms it. `chatCleanup.pendingRequests/observedAt=null` means unknown, not zero.

Register using `POST /v2/app` with `{"name":"StemWise"}` or `{"name":"Studywell"}`. GET/PUT settings and prompt routes are scoped to this installation. Read `/v2/codex/models` and its pagination rather than hard-coding the model used in bridge tests. The complete route table and schemas are in `documentation.md`.

Wake: an explicit user Wake, Send to Bridge, Retry or settings Wake action may authorize one `POST /v2/connection/wake` with `""` as the body when needed. Durably claim at most one attempt for that action before the call, independently of the immutable job envelope; never replay that claim after timeout or restart. A new explicit user action may authorize a new attempt. Passive polling, reconnect, startup, job execution, agents, background recovery and automatic retries never authorize wake. The Pi sees an authenticated empty request, not the UI action or app-local claim; this boundary belongs in the app. HTTP 202 proves packet submission only. Observe fresh connection status afterward; wake authorization never authorizes resubmitting uncertain jobs.

## Immutable jobs and streaming files

1. Keep drafts and approval in app-owned storage. Before any song input upload or job submission, obtain explicit per-song approval in StemWise. Allocate a fresh 32-character lowercase hex job ID and capture the current Unix time in milliseconds. Preserve the original `text` and `instructions` HTTP fields. Capture `model`, `effort` (intelligence) and `serviceTier` (speed) from the selected model's live catalog. Empty/omitted/null values inherit saved app choices at first admission, then native defaults; use explicit advertised values to bind a reviewed choice. To bypass a saved tier for this job, persist `nativeDefaultServiceTier:true` with an absent/empty/null tier instead. Do not label inheritance or native unset policy as verified Standard.
2. Call `client.openAppFiles(operationId, PI_HOST, PI_ID)` after app registration. For each source, call `files.prepareFile(operationId, displayName, absoluteSourcePath)` to create a managed immutable snapshot. If the app starts from an Android content URI, copy it through the app's granted content resolver into an app-owned regular file first; no broad-storage permission is required.
3. Persist the complete approved immutable job JSON, including all three choices, and exact returned input descriptors atomically in the app's existing durable outbox **before** submitting. Persist transfer IDs before sending. Use `files.ensureSent(operationToken, originalTransferId)` both initially and after restart: it returns the exact existing committed receipt or sends that same immutable snapshot only after a fresh authenticated absence response. Corrupt, uncertain or malformed receipts never authorize an upload. One reserved operation owns this entire probe/send phase. Preserve snapshots during unresolved retries. The separate `send` and read-only `receipt` methods remain available when the app explicitly owns their separate phases.
4. POST the immutable envelope to `/v2/jobs`. HTTP 202 queues work even while the PC or its Codex login is unavailable. Preserve the original ID, sender createdAt and unchanged envelope. The Pi receiver's returned created starts a fixed three-day deadline for every job state; expiresAt is authoritative, and delivery/retry never extends it. Persist verified outputs into app-owned storage before expiry. On uncertain acceptance observe the original ID. A 404 job_unavailable is not permission to replay: resolve tracking with an empty-body POST `/v2/jobs/<original-id>/retire`, preserving a 200 retained job or persisting its 410 request_deleted replay barrier. Expiry does not claim physical native stop. Storage/capacity/transport errors keep the request unresolved. Reads/resume never request wake.
5. Poll the original job with bounded observation. Show native transport state and the separate developer report/log. Timeout ends observation, not the server job. On app restart, restore the original durable context and observe it. Unknown native dispatch must never be replayed as new work.
6. Once the complete verified output batch is published, use `receiveMatching(operationId, id, name, size, sha256)` for each exact descriptor. Copy it to a new app-owned destination with `copyReceived(operationId, id, absoluteDestination)`. This copies into an exact transfer/destination-owned sibling stage, verifies size/hash, syncs it and publishes a complete file atomically without overwrite. Use an app-private destination. Android/Linux publishes with an atomic non-replacing rename; Windows uses a non-replacing move. Filesystems or platforms lacking that operation fail explicitly; there is no overwriting fallback. No partial file is exposed at the final path, even if the app process dies mid-copy. A retry for the same original transfer ID and destination removes its abandoned stage and recopies the verified local inbox without networking or resubmitting the job. An existing final is always refused, including matching bytes; reconcile its actual size/hash before deciding it was previously imported. Never overwrite or delete a conflicting destination blindly.
7. Atomically save the app's import/result state. Call `client.confirmDelivery(operationId, PI_HOST, PI_ID, jobId, importsJson)` with the complete ordered batch: `[{"file":{"id":"...","name":"...","size":123,"sha256":"..."},"path":"/absolute/app/import"}]`. The SDK hashes the actual destination files before acknowledging. For jobs with no outputs, pass `[]` after saving the successful result. Acknowledgment is idempotent; it may report chat cleanup pending while native deletion retries. Do not resubmit the job. The SDK pins every opened destination and its shared copy/delivery claim through the synchronous acknowledgment, and rechecks exact path-to-file identity after hashing the complete batch and after the reply. Keep the app's import-root ownership/exclusion until confirmDelivery actually returns; Unix descriptors do not prevent an independent app thread or process from renaming or rewriting a path. A conflicting SDK destination owner returns delivery_destination_in_use. A changed path detected before sending returns delivery_destination_unverified; a change detected after the request returns delivery_destination_changed_acknowledgment_unconfirmed. The latter may already have a remote delivery receipt: reconcile the original job instead of replaying or replacing it. The SDK preserves existing app files.
8. After delivery, discard prepared/received bridge snapshots using `discardPrepared`/`removeReceived` when no longer needed. Keep imported app-owned copies. DELETE a terminal job when appropriate; disconnection removes only this installation's bridge data and rejects active/uncertain work. Do not treat disconnect/re-enrollment as retry recovery.

For an approved `UNSENT` request that has never been submitted, the app may restore an expired local prepared snapshot from its retained app-owned source using `files.restorePreparedFile(operationId, exactDescriptorJson, absoluteSourcePath)`. Use the original descriptor's exact ID, name, size and SHA-256 and keep the approved request unchanged; do not call `prepareFile` to allocate a replacement ID. This local-only call verifies a regular source file, snapshots the exact bytes and refuses invalid descriptors, changed bytes and conflicting cache objects. It requires no enrollment or network access. A matching existing snapshot keeps its original local expiry; an expired/missing local snapshot can be recreated. The call never contacts the Pi, submits a job or refreshes any remote deadline. The app's durable request journal owns the `UNSENT` decision: the SDK cannot infer job acceptance from a file descriptor. Never use restoration to resume `UNKNOWN`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, accepted or expired jobs; observe the original job instead. After local restoration, the existing `ensureSent` receipt/absence checks still apply before first submission. Keep the source in app-owned storage outside the SDK's managed directory, and use a fresh operation token for each phase. The descriptor JSON is strict, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, with exactly `id`, `name`, `size` and `sha256`. The returned JSON preserves those values, not input whitespace/key order; compare parsed fields and retain the original approved envelope. `BridgeUsage.restoreUnsentInput` shows the binding.

Files are opaque; bridge code does not unpack ZIPs or parse FLAC/PNG/JSON. Use safe app-owned destination names rather than trusting a descriptor as a filesystem path. Streaming limit: 1 GiB per file, 16 declared files per job, 30-minute transfer window. `prepare(operationId,name,byte[])`/`readReceived(operationId,id)` are convenience APIs capped at 64 MiB; do not use them for large archives. Two Pi downloads may run simultaneously; a capacity rejection requires retry of the same descriptor, never another job.

Apps keep the existing HTTP job envelope and immutable hashes. The bridge constructs exactly one native user input of type `text`, containing `bridgeJobInput:v1` JSON: `prompt` and `customInstructions` preserve the original fields verbatim, including links. Its `handoffPath`, `handoffSha256`, ten-field authenticated `handoffHeader` and `readBeforeWork` direct the agent to read and hash-verify the full real local Markdown before any task work. The full workflow, current job IDs, file descriptors and runtime paths remain in that file; they are not inlined or sent as extra text/mention inputs or native `developerInstructions`. Each fresh job still owns one chat and uses the same strict report contract. Only top-level bridgeJobReport messages claim a result/error report; raw commentary is never exported. Job/list progress is a separate nullable advisory object with stage, source:commentary_marker, formatting:plain|normalized|unrecognized and observedAt. Stages are preparing, reading, processing, testing, packaging, transferring, waiting or unknown. The injected MD requires one exact reserved token such as [[bridge:testing]] as the entire plain-text progress message while the agent continues the same turn. The parser tolerates simple Markdown around one token but labels it normalized; ordinary words/prose and embedded or quoted tokens do not trigger progress; malformed explicit token claims become unknown. Render this as inferred stage detail, never as verified completion or an error, and preserve the authoritative state/report/output checks. No new Android method or signature is needed. Authoritative terminal history, a valid terminal report and independently verified outputs remain required. Apps need not combine messages or supply a handoff path.

`serviceTiers:null` means the native capability is unknown; an empty array confirms no explicit choices. Each advertised option has an exact `id`, `name` and `description`; `defaultServiceTier` may be null. Never substitute a guessed tier or silently clear a saved tier when a model changes. Explicit `"default"` is supported only if listed. A resolved tier requires a selected or saved model (`400 service_tier_model_required`). Unconfirmed capability keeps the job queued; a confirmed unsupported choice rejects it. Job reads expose captured `model`, `effort`, `serviceTier`; the input endpoint retains submitted choices without backfilling saved defaults (empty/omitted/null normalize equivalently). Existing IDs retain these choices across retries/restart/settings changes. The SDK forwards ordinary JSON; there is no new Java runtime method or SDK-owned draft/approval database. `BridgeUsage.newJob` includes the tier in its immutable envelope. Current choices are requested configuration, not verified effective speed. Read `documentation.md` before implementing settings PUT: it replaces all saved choices rather than patching only present fields.

The per-job boolean `nativeDefaultServiceTier:true` overrides only tier inheritance: absent/empty/null `serviceTier` captures an empty tier and omits the native override even if the app saved a priority tier. It leaves model/effort resolution unchanged. True with a nonempty tier returns `400 invalid_service_tier_choice`; omitted/false/null keeps the existing inheritance and hashes of requests without this flag. Other flag types return `400 invalid_job`. For example, add `{"model":"gpt-6-luna","effort":"max","nativeDefaultServiceTier":true}` as choices in the complete immutable envelope, subject to live model/effort support. Persist and retry that flag unchanged; the original input retains it, and changing it on an accepted ID returns `409 request_id_conflict`. It is not a settings PUT field or a claim of Standard/Fast. Apps can add the boolean to their ordinary job JSON; no new SDK method is required.

The job view additionally exposes `cancelReason`: `user_request` for new user cancellation, `native_interaction_required` for the unattended guard, or empty only when no cancellation has been requested. Both paths persist intent and require exact background retirement before terminal stop is confirmed; automatic stops retain their independent diagnostic and interrupted status. Observation/settings-validation cancellation follows the HTTP caller, while already accepted jobs and mutation receipts remain service-owned.

For an explicit user Cancel action, POST `/v2/jobs/<id>/cancel`. A provably unsent accepted queued job returns 200 cancelled with cancelRequested/cancelRetired recorded together; cancelAcknowledged may remain zero because no native interruption was needed. Repeating cancel or the original immutable submission preserves that receipt. An active or uncertain submission saves intent and returns 202. Poll the original job rather than resubmitting it. `cancelRequested`, `cancelAcknowledged` and `cancelRetired` are receiver timestamps, with zero meaning unobserved. An interrupt acknowledgment alone is not a terminal cancellation: the bridge also verifies the original terminal turn and exact owned background execution retirement. While unavailable, display pending/uncertain cancellation and its separate job diagnostics. A missing job without a retained receipt returns 404 job_unavailable; use the explicit retire resolution above, never mark it cancelled/stopped from absence. A retained admission barrier returns 410 request_deleted, which retires tracking with historical execution unknown. Latch cancellation locally before scheduling and never submit after that latch. Already terminal completed jobs return their existing result, preserving installed app media; cancelRequested may remain zero, so do not wait for cancellation timestamps on a pre-existing terminal result. Cancelling a local operation token or worker only ends observation/local IO; it does not replace this server request.

Explicit retirement retains only the absent request ID and a 72-hour deadline from that action; it does not extend job/content retention. Repeated retire, GET, cancel, delivery and DELETE do not renew an existing receipt. While retained, GET/submission/cancel/delivery/retire return 410 request_deleted; DELETE returns 200 deleted:true and preserves the barrier. After automatic receipt pruning, bare 404 is uncertain again and an unresolved local request can explicitly establish a new bounded barrier. The backend cannot permanently reject an arbitrary frozen request after all its receipt evidence has been deleted; the app must persist retirement and never resubmit that work, including after restart/disconnection. Never clear local imported files/journals merely because tracking is forgotten. `BridgeUsage.retireUnresolvedJob` shows the call; documentation.md specifies errors, serialization and preservation.

Metadata listings and remote output `info` read stored commit metadata without rehashing every payload. Actual reads, upload receipts, output publication, local import and delivery verification still check the consumed bytes. `receivedInfo` remains an explicit byte-verification operation. File pages can include at most 16 structural `diagnostics` plus the total `diagnosticCount`; display the omitted count rather than assuming the samples are complete. `files.storageDiagnostics(operationToken)` reads bounded incoming/outgoing issues for this exact paired identity. Explicit `discardPrepared`/`removeReceived` can discard a damaged owned local object without trusting its old descriptor; never invoke discard as an automatic retry repair. The Pi's own scoped issues are in `data.storageDiagnostics` from `GET /v2/connection`. An unresolved damaged Pi object prevents disconnect from silently deleting its registration/ownership context.

All Bridge jobs expire 72 hours after receiver-owned job.created, including queued, active, failed, uncertain and undelivered work. Pi records/reports/logs and final-owner managed file bytes are removed at expiry, independently of delivery or PC connectivity. A compact bounded exact-owner cleanup outbox retries PC cleanup; expiredJobCleanup and chatCleanup distinguish outstanding work from confirmed physical deletion. A powered-off or unreadable device cleans up when available and must not be shown as already erased. The PC independently ages its receiver-committed owned creation, rejects late output publication, journals retirement/deletion and keeps minimal unresolved cleanup ownership. Native closure/replay receipts expire after a further bounded 72 hours. Explicit terminal DELETE remains separate early discard and can return retryable job_cleanup_authorization_unconfirmed while preserving a job that has not reached its fixed deadline. Existing Android SDK disposable cache rules are unchanged. App-owned imported files, ZIP/import journals, saved prompts, settings and enrollment persist; no Bridge cleanup deletes them. Download again only from an unexpired original job; never run a replacement job to recover an expired local cache.

Existing Client.status and FileClient.storageDiagnostics JSON now include backgroundOperations.file_retention. Each incoming/outgoing diagnostic page adds observedAt (Unix milliseconds, or null before observation) from existing maintenance. Routine status/file requests do not scan unrelated history. Use storageDiagnostics for offline, read-only observation; it does not start transport or trigger cleanup. Read failureActive and the latest bounded failure cause/time separately from transport connection and per-job results. Successful recovery clears failureActive while retaining the last observation in memory. Store scan failure uses storage_diagnostics_unavailable with a null diagnosticCount instead of a healthy zero. See documentation.md for the common background-pass fields and retry-policy semantics.

Per-file cache access checks the requested object's expiry and shape without sweeping both stores. Startup and the existing worker perform full cleanup; explicit DiscardPrepared/RemoveReceived remain available. Once the stores and ownership lease open safely, a startup cleanup failure stays visible in file_retention status and retries after one minute without blocking healthy objects. Store-open and lease failures still prevent initialization. Expired cached objects stay unavailable before that worker runs, while failure in an unrelated store does not block a healthy object's operation. Public SDK signatures and transport/receipt validation are unchanged. No device timing or battery benefit has been measured.

## Background execution

The Pi continues accepted work without the app or PC being connected; actual execution waits for the PC. Use the app's own durable scheduler to resume observation, verified local import and deferred delivery acknowledgment. BridgeRecovery exposes only the shared client factory; there are no service start/stop/state/requestOnce APIs. Keep cancellation latched across scheduled phases, preserve original request/transfer IDs, and never use recovery callbacks to wake the PC or replay work. Connection observations expire independently of durable jobs.

Power controls use the existing JSON HTTP transport. A user wake request can return HTTP 202 with packet_sent/unconfirmed, wake_coalesced/unconfirmed or already_on/reachable; only packet_sent claims a new packet. Read GET /v2/connection/power (also power in connection/wake replies) for the shared cycle, investigation hold and bounded aggregate job counts. A manually powered PC remains unmanaged. Only an OS boot/resume correlated with an explicit Bridge wake can arm automatic graceful shutdown. All apps' pending work and verified output delivery must drain first; confirmed user cancellations also require actual native cleanup. A one-minute stable drain prevents immediate power cycling. New jobs receive 409 power_shutdown_pending after shutdown commitment; preserve their immutable envelope and require a fresh user action for any later wake. Do not translate that error into an automatic wake loop.

An investigation hold survives job expiry and service restart without retaining the job's content beyond 72 hours. After the user investigates and explicitly discards or resolves the affected job, POST /v2/connection/power/release with the exact current cycleId acknowledges the hold; other unresolved jobs still prevent release/shutdown. Apps may connect this acknowledgment to an explicit user Revoke action after its exact job cleanup succeeds. Never clear a hold from passive recovery. A recorded shutdown acknowledgment remains a requested outcome; loss of reachability alone cannot prove physical power-off, and no app may replay a shutdown attempt. BridgeUsage includes powerStatus and releasePowerHold examples. No Android SDK method or signature changed.

## Status and debugging

Keep `state`, `report.status`, `outputs`, `delivered`, `chatState` and `/log` separate. In particular, `state=completed` with a missing/invalid terminal report or `output_bytes_unverified` is an unconfirmed task outcome. Preserve exact job ID, code, structured diagnostic and stage for investigation. Show useful action text inside the app; do not display native conversation or ask the user to execute terminal commands. Retryable describes the indicated read/transfer/recovery action, not permission to repeat the original task. The bridge's creation_not_sent and creation_rejected diagnostics keep the same queued job: recovery observes its original reservation and requires authenticated absence before retrying unchanged creation. Apps must continue observing the original ID rather than resubmitting or generating a replacement.

The source/SDK update for APP-03 also adds operationId as the first argument of pending, received and receivedInfo. Do not generate the ID inside an inaccessible helper: the app must own it so cancellation can reach the actual synchronous work. Explicit cache cleanup methods remain separate. SOURCE_BUILD.md documents cancellation limits and TOOL-03 source-build/promotion paths.

Known-ID cache lookup: call `files.receivedInfo(operationId,transferId)` directly. Verified success is `{state:"received_local_verified",pcIdentity,file}`; genuine local absence is `{state:"absent",pcIdentity,transferId}` with no file. Validate pcIdentity against the identity used to open this FileClient (PI_ID for openAppFiles, PC_ID only for direct PC files) and validate the descriptor/requested transfer identity. Only the absent result permits downloading that same original transfer. Corrupt/unreadable/closed/cancelled state remains an error, never an absence inference from inventory or exception text.

For offline recovery after a verified download but interrupted app import, obtain the shared client, then call `client.localFiles(PI_HOST, PI_ID)`. `receivedInfo`, `received`, `copyReceived`, `storageDiagnostics`, `removeReceived` and `discardPrepared` use local storage without starting the node. Do not call `status`, `openAppFiles` or another remote readiness method as a prerequisite. A cancelled copy removes its unpublished sibling stage and preserves the verified cached source until its original cache deadline; reopening or reading never extends that deadline. The SDK holds the node storage lease until actual copy cleanup retires, including during client close, so a reopened client cannot reclaim a live copier's stage. Copying twice concurrently to the same destination is refused as received_copy_in_use. A malformed non-regular reserved stage is refused as received_copy_stage_invalid. The app owns its import journal and destination folder; retry the original ID/path to clean an interrupted stage, or clean the abandoned app-owned import folder when that import is discarded. Preserve the app-owned import journal and verify any already existing destination instead of overwriting it. After the complete output batch is durably imported, defer `confirmDelivery` until approved connectivity returns; local verification/copy never acknowledges remote delivery or deletes the remote output.
